prize_parts.citation: For introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into the theory of international trade, and for showing how reallocation across firms shapes exporting, foreign investment and the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B001 alone, credited to Helpman and Melitz. I tried to break it in this round and it held on merit, maturity and exact credit. Merit: Melitz (2003) and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple (2004) replaced the representative-firm view with selection of heterogeneous firms into exporting and foreign investment. This made reallocation across firms a first-order channel for the gains from trade and produced sorting predictions that could be confronted with firm-level data. From my own field I weigh most heavily the question of what is identified. Here the mechanism yields implications beyond the facts that motivated it, namely the exports-versus-FDI sorting result and the reallocation channel. The record shows these implications being confirmed in part and rejected in part, which is a sign of a research programme that did real work. Maturity: the core papers are more than twenty years old and have been tested and extended across many datasets. Exact credit: the canonical selection model is Melitz's, and the FDI-sorting extension and the monopolistic-competition foundations bring Helpman in. I considered a second part, since the chair asked about it. Under the three-person cap B001 already uses two names, so any second part could carry only one person. A one-person B006 would fragment the Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes credit, and a one-person B030 would misrepresent a multi-author body of work. A single-part, two-name prize is therefore the only configuration I can defend. I have narrowed the citation to the selection and reallocation framework. It makes no claim about the size of the welfare gains and no claim to the empirical exporter-premia facts or the quantitative-trade lineage. My alternatives are reordered to B006 then B030. The attribution and boundary arguments in round 1 persuaded me that, if B001 failed on attribution grounds, B006's three-name BLP core is a cleaner fallback than B030's split between the task framework and the China-shock evidence. My own opening rank for B030 is not a merit argument for placing it first. I do not treat the unanimity of round-1 files as evidence of merit, and the chair rightly notes that shared reasoning patterns could inflate it.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection remains attribution at the edges. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum made closely related and in part parallel contributions, including the exporter-premia facts, and they are not credited on this ballot entry. A two-person award could be read as under-crediting a wider lineage. Redding is credited on the ballot but is not in my pair, so a broader framing of the discovery as quantitative trade would raise his claim. The baseline Melitz model is rejected in some details, and its welfare conclusions depend on distributional and functional-form assumptions. Much of its lasting influence therefore comes from extensions. Helpman's earlier monopolistic-competition work also sits near the lineage recognised in 2008, so a Committee could judge that part of his credit is already covered. I also hold this ballot to the same standard I would apply to a measurement-heavy field: a prize should not be read as endorsing quantitative magnitudes that the evidence does not settle.

responses.point: Hassler moved from B006 first to B001 first, keeps B006 as his first alternative, and notes that the five credited people across B001 and B006 exceed the three-person limit. A trimmed pairing such as Pakes alone would fragment the BLP credit. He ties the citation to the theoretical selection mechanism and says the empirical precursors can be acknowledged in the scientific background.
responses.response: I agree that combining the two is not feasible, and I tested it for that reason: any second part would carry at most one name, and a one-name B006 misstates who made the BLP contribution. I accept that the empirical precursors can be acknowledged in the background rather than credited. I would add one condition. Acknowledgement in the background does not repair the citation, so the wording itself must not imply that the prize covers the exporter-premia facts or the quantitative magnitudes. That is why my citation names selection and reallocation and says nothing about the size of the gains. I also take your point that B006 is a credible fallback and I have moved it ahead of B030 in my alternatives.

responses.point: Enflo treats the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as more than a caveat. If the discovery is read as the empirical facts plus the theory, the credited names are incomplete, and the prize recognises the model that organised those facts. She notes that this is a judgment about what counts as the discovery, and she wants the citation to name selection and firm heterogeneity and not trade theory generically.
responses.response: I agree with the citation point and have worded mine that way. On the judgment itself, my test is whether the theory generated implications beyond the facts that motivated it. The exports-versus-FDI sorting result and the reallocation channel for the gains from trade are such implications. They are not restatements of exporter premia, which supports treating the model as the discovery and the facts as its empirical motivation. I still think this is a judgment, as you say, and that the record does not settle it. I would count the exclusion of the empirical pioneers as a real cost of this configuration and not describe it as costless. For me it is outweighed by the cleaner discovery boundary. If a majority read the discovery as the whole firm-level programme, I would regard that as a legitimate reason to prefer a different candidate, not to widen B001 beyond the credited names.

responses.point: Fredriksson says the China-shock design is the quasi-experimental evidence he finds most convincing, but that it identifies local labour-market adjustment, which is narrower than the task-based claims about technology. Combining the two strands in one citation would overstate how far one body of evidence supports the other. If the Committee chose a labour-market prize he would favour Autor, Hanson and Katz, with the Dorn-versus-Katz caveat stated openly.
responses.response: I agree that the two strands should not be merged under one citation, and your point is part of why I now put B030 behind B006 in my alternatives. The identification question is what moves me. The China-shock evidence is credible for what it identifies, but the task framework rests on a different kind of evidence, and the credit for it extends beyond the names on the ballot, with a Katz overlap with the 2023 prize noted by Dreber Almenberg. A fallback should be a configuration I can describe in one sentence without stretching the evidence, and I can do that more easily for the BLP core. I would keep B030 as a genuine alternative, narrowed to the trade-shock evidence if it ever advanced.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee reads the discovery as the selection and reallocation model (Helpman and Melitz) or as the broader firm-level and quantitative trade programme, which would strengthen the claims of Redding, and of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum who are not on the ballot entry.

How much of Helpman's credit overlaps with the monopolistic-competition lineage recognised in 2008, and whether that should narrow the weight placed on his foundations as opposed to the FDI-sorting result.
How far the sensitivity of the baseline welfare implications to distributional assumptions should limit the citation. I have deliberately kept the citation silent on welfare magnitudes.
Whether the B006 boundary can be settled as demand estimation only (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) or must include the dynamic-games strand, since that decides whether it is a clean fallback.
My assessments rest on the supplied round-1 files, the chair's summary and general knowledge. I have not independently verified citation counts, priority records or award histories.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure. My profile shows co-authorship with Torsten Persson and Bo Rothstein (a corruption paper in Governance), and Persson is a credited name on B038. I also gave the 2024 presentation speech on institutions and prosperity, which is thematically adjacent to B038. B038 is in neither my preferred configuration nor my alternatives, so none of this bears on my proposal. No connection to Helpman, Melitz, Redding or the credited names on B006 and B030 is apparent from the supplied profile. At Stockholm University I am a colleague of Hassler, Krusell and Boppart but in a different department, and none of them is a candidate on B001, B006 or B030. My background in political-science measurement and datasets (QoG, V-Dem) may incline me to scrutinise what evidence a prize claim rests on and how credit is bounded. I disclose that as a methodological disposition and not as a tie, and I do not adjudicate it.
